questions.title: What if your friend moves your ball when looking for it?
questions.question: You and your friend are playing a match. Your ball is lost in the long grass (the rough), and while your friend is helping to look, they accidentally move your ball. What should you do?

choices.text: Your friend gets a penalty and the ball goes back where it was
No one gets a penalty, and you must put the ball back where it was
Play the ball from where it ended up
You get a penalty and must put the ball back where it was

questions.explanation: If your friend moves your ball by accident while helping you find it, no one gets a penalty. You must put your ball back where it was before it was moved.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Match play is when you and a friend compete to win each hole.
Rough means the long grass next to the fairway on a golf course.

questions.teachingTip: Demonstrate searching for a ball in the rough and show how to mark and replace a moved ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think someone always gets a penalty when a ball is moved.
They may think the ball can be played from its new spot.

questions.title: Opponent moves your ball in match play
questions.question: In match play, your opponent accidentally moves your ball while searching for it in the rough. What is the correct procedure?

choices.text: Your opponent gets a penalty and the ball is replaced
No penalty for anyone, and the ball must be replaced
The ball is played from its new position
You get a penalty and must replace the ball

questions.explanation: In match play, if your opponent moves your ball accidentally during a search, no one is penalised but the ball must be put back where it was.
